test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: An urn initially contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. You draw two balls without replacement. If both balls are the same color, you stop. If they are different colors, you put both balls back into the urn, add one additional red ball to the urn, and then draw two more balls. What is the probability that you do not stop on the first draw, but you stop on the second draw?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First draw different = (3×2 + 2×3) ÷ (5×4) = 12/20 = 3/5

Add 1 red → new balls = 4R, 2B (total 6)

Second draw same color = [4C2 + 2C2] ÷ 6C2 = (6 + 1)/15 = 7/15

Required probability = 3/5 × 7/15

= 21/75 = 7/25

**∴ Answer = 7/25**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial: 3 red, 2 blue

Condition: Stop if same color, else add 1 red and repeat

**Formula used:**

Probability = Favorable outcomes ÷ Total outcomes

**Calculations:**

⇒ P(different first) = (3×2 + 2×3) ÷ (5×4) = 12 ÷ 20 = 3/5

⇒ New urn: 4 red, 2 blue → total = 6

⇒ P(same second) = [4C2 + 2C2] ÷ 6C2 = (6 + 1) ÷ 15 = 7/15

⇒ Required probability = 3/5 × 7/15 = 21/75 = 7/25

**∴ The correct answer is 7/25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Without Replacement

Probabilities change after each draw since total balls reduce

Combination Formula

nC2 = n(n−1)/2 used for selecting 2 items

Sequential Probability

Multiply probabilities of successive independent steps

Same Color Cases

Same color = both red or both blue → add both probabilities
